bib.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can language-model inference be improved on tasks needing exploration, lookahead or backtracking by searching over a tree of coherent intermediate text units (thoughts) with the LM itself generating and evaluating them?
hypothesis: Left-to-right token-level decoding (IO, CoT, CoT-SC) is a 'System 1' mechanism that fails on search/planning tasks; adding a deliberate 'System 2' search with LM self-evaluation, lookahead and backtracking will do markedly better.
contributions: The Tree of Thoughts framework: generalizes IO, CoT, CoT-SC and self-refinement as special cases, modular over thought decomposition, generator, state evaluator and search algorithm, no extra training.
Three new tasks that challenge GPT-4 (Game of 24, Creative Writing, Mini Crosswords) with ToT results and ablations.
LM self-evaluation as a third kind of search heuristic, alongside programmed (Deep Blue) and learned (AlphaGo).

method.summary: ToT prompts a pre-trained chat LM to propose or sample k candidate next thoughts from each state, evaluate states by value prompts (sure/maybe/impossible, or 1-10) or by voting, and runs BFS (keep best b states per step) or DFS (prune below a value threshold, backtrack). Instantiated per task: Game of 24 with BFS b=5, Creative Writing with a depth-2 sample-and-vote tree, Mini Crosswords with DFS and pruning. No training of any kind.
method.task: Search/planning problems with an LLM: arithmetic puzzle, constrained creative writing, 5x5 mini crosswords

datasets.name: Game of 24 (4nums.com)
datasets.split: games indexed 901-1,000 (relatively hard, sorted by human solving time)

datasets.name: Mini Crosswords (GooBix)
datasets.split: 20 test games (indices 1, 6, ..., 91, 96); games 136, 141, 146, 151, 156 used for prompting
datasets.preprocessing: adjacent games contain similar clues, hence the spaced test indices

other.note: main model; experiments done between May 5-16, 2023; exact snapshot not stated
appendix B.2 only; Game of 24 proposal prompt changed from 1-shot to 3-shot

inference.samples: Game of 24: IO and CoT sampled 100 times per game, CoT-SC majority of 100 CoT samples, IO+Refine up to 10 iterations. Creative Writing: 10 IO and 10 CoT samples per task, refine k<=5, GPT-4 score averaged over 5 scores per output. Crosswords: 10 samples per prompt, averaged. Single run of ToT; no seeds or variance reported.
inference.prompting: Game of 24 IO: 5 in-context examples; CoT adds 3 intermediate equations per example; ToT propose prompt has one 4-number example, same prompt for all 3 steps. Creative Writing IO and CoT zero-shot. Crosswords IO 5 examples, CoT adds intermediate words h1..5 then v1..5.

parameters.game_of_24: 3 thought steps; BFS keep b=5 (b=1 also run); propose prompt per state; value prompt labels each thought sure/maybe/impossible, sampled 3 times per thought
parameters.creative_writing: depth 2, one intermediate thought (plan); 5 plans sampled i.i.d. then 5 votes; 5 passages then 5 votes; b=1
parameters.mini_crosswords: DFS, thoughts constrained not to change filled words so at most 10 intermediate steps; proposal prompt sampled 5 times, with LM confidence levels aggregated into a priority queue; state evaluator marks each remaining clue possible/impossible and prunes if any is impossible; DFS limited to 100 steps; deepest explored state (first if tied) rendered as output
parameters.bfs_general: BFS used when depth T<=3 and breadth b<=5
parameters.zero_shot_tot_B1: GSM8K/StrategyQA: sample 5 strategies, vote for best; sample 5 solutions, vote for best

other.vote_aggregation: prompt LM multiple times and aggregate value or vote results

metrics.name: Game of 24 success rate
metrics.definition: output is a valid equation equal to 24 using the input numbers each exactly once, over 100 games

metrics.name: Creative Writing coherency score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 zero-shot 1-10 scalar score, 5 samples averaged per output

metrics.name: Creative Writing human comparison
metrics.definition: blind pairwise coherency comparison of CoT vs ToT passages by a subset of authors, order randomly flipped, over 100 inputs

metrics.name: Mini Crosswords success
metrics.definition: portion of correct letters (25 per game), words (10 per game) and games solved

baselines: IO + Refine (k=10, uses ground-truth correctness feedback)
eval.protocol: Single ToT run per task. Creative Writing human study uses a subset of the authors, not independent raters. Standard deviation of the 5 GPT-4 scores about 0.56 on average. No significance tests.

prompts.purpose: Zero-shot voting prompt for ToT on GSM8K/StrategyQA
prompts.text: Given an instruction and several choices, decide which choice is most promising. Analyze each choice in detail, then conclude in the last line "The best choice is {s}", where s the integer id of the choice.

prompts.purpose: Zero-shot CoT/ToT thought format for GSM8K/StrategyQA
prompts.text:
Answer the following question: {input}
Make a strategy then write. Your output should be of the following format:
Strategy:
Your strategy about how to answer the question.
Answer:
Your answer to the question. It should end with {format}.

prompts.purpose: Creative Writing vote prompt (paraphrased in text)
prompts.text: analyze choices below, then conclude which is most promising for the instruction

results.claim: On Game of 24, ToT with breadth 5 solves 74% of games.
results.setup: GPT-4 chat, temperature 0.7, games 901-1,000 of 4nums.com, BFS b=5, 3 thought steps, value prompt sampled 3 times per thought, single run
results.quote: achieves a success rate of 45%, while b = 5 achieves 74%.
results.note: Abstract says CoT solved 4%; Table 2 prints 4.0%.

results.claim: IO, CoT and CoT-SC prompting perform badly on Game of 24.
results.setup: GPT-4, Game of 24 games 901-1,000; CoT prompted with 3 intermediate equations, averaged over 100 samples per game; IO 7.3%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%

results.claim: ToT with breadth 1 (no beam) already reaches 45% on Game of 24.
results.quote: achieves a success rate of 45%, while b = 5 achieves 74%.

results.claim: Oracle best of 100 CoT samples reaches 49% on Game of 24, still well below ToT b=5.
results.setup: GPT-4, Game of 24; best-of-k oracle (any of 100 samples correct) treated as visiting k nodes; IO best of 100 is 33%
results.table: Table 2, row CoT (best of 100), column Success
results.note: The oracle uses ground-truth correctness to pick the best sample, so it is not a deployable baseline.

results.claim: IO + Refine (up to 10 iterations, with ground-truth feedback) reaches 27% on Game of 24.
results.setup: GPT-4, Game of 24, refine conditioned on all previous history, uses groundtruth feedback on equation correctness
results.table: Table 2, row IO + Refine (k=10), column Success

results.claim: Around 60% of CoT samples on Game of 24 had already failed after the first step.
results.metric: share of CoT samples failed at step 1
results.setup: GPT-4, Game of 24, CoT samples; failure means the thought is invalid or cannot reach 24; value read as approximate
results.quote: around 60% of CoT samples already failed the task after generating the first step

results.claim: In Creative Writing ToT gets a higher GPT-4 coherency score than IO and CoT.
results.setup: GPT-4 generating and scoring, 100 inputs, 5 scores averaged per output; ToT = 5 plans + vote, 5 passages + vote, b=1; scorer is the same model family as the generator

results.claim: Authors prefer ToT over CoT passages in 41 of 100 pairs, CoT over ToT in 21, tie in 38.

results.claim: Iterative refine raises Creative Writing coherency for IO from 6.19 to 7.67 and ToT from 7.56 to 7.91.

results.quote: it improves IO coherency score from 6.19 to 7.67, and ToT coherency score from 7.56 to 7.91.

results.claim: On Mini Crosswords ToT reaches 60% word-level success and solves 4 of 20 games, against 14-15.6% word success for IO/CoT.
results.setup: GPT-4, 20 test games, DFS limited to 100 steps, pruning on; IO/CoT 10 samples averaged; letter-level 78% vs 38.7/40.6
results.quote: success rate of 60% and solving 4 out of 20 games.
results.note: Table 3 columns are Letter, Word, Game; IO game-level 0%, CoT 1%, ToT 20%.

results.claim: Choosing the oracle best DFS state instead of the heuristic one lifts crosswords to 7 of 20 games.
results.setup: GPT-4, Mini Crosswords, ToT '+best state' oracle

results.setup: GPT-4, Mini Crosswords, ToT with pruning removed
results.note: Without pruning it still found the solution in 4/20 games but only output 1 via the heuristic.

limits: Authors: deliberate search may be unnecessary for tasks GPT-4 already handles (Appendix B.1); only three relatively simple tasks were tried.
Authors: ToT needs more resources (GPT-4 API cost) than sampling methods; 5-100x more generated tokens than CoT.
Authors: off-the-shelf LM only; fine-tuning for ToT-style deliberation left open.
Authors: state evaluator is imperfect; GPT-4 pruned valid but rare/obsolete words in crosswords (example 'agend').
Best-of-k IO/CoT baselines are oracles; IO+Refine uses ground-truth feedback.
Single run per configuration, no variance or significance tests; Creative Writing human study uses authors as judges and GPT-4 judges GPT-4 output.
Tasks and prompts were designed by the authors to challenge GPT-4 as of May 2023; later reasoning models do much of this search internally (not in the paper).
Only BFS and DFS explored; A* and MCTS left for future work.

terms.definition: a coherent language sequence that serves as an intermediate step toward problem solving
maintains a set of the b most promising states per step (Algorithm 1)
explores the most promising state first until the output is reached or the evaluator deems it impossible (value <= threshold), then prunes and backtracks (Algorithm 2)
